title: Diversification
concept: Diversification means spreading money across different investments and asset types so financial results do not depend too heavily on one company or outcome.
learningObjective: Understand how spreading money across different investments can reduce concentration risk without eliminating the possibility of loss.
primaryMisconception: Diversification guarantees that an investor will not lose money.
secondaryMisconceptions: Owning several investments from the same company or industry provides complete diversification.
Diversification always produces higher returns than concentrating money in one investment.
keyTakeaway: Diversification reduces concentration risk but does not remove all risk.

screens.title: Everything Riding on One Result
screens.content: You put Rs. 10,000 into one company. One bad announcement arrives. How much of your plan depends on that single result?
screens.illustration: Ten Rs. 1,000 tokens balance on one company card while a warning notification appears above it.

screens.title: Your Rs. 10,000 Choice
screens.content: You have Rs. 10,000 available for a fictional investment plan. You can place it in one company or spread it across several choices.
screens.illustration: Ten Rs. 1,000 tokens sit beside four empty allocation sections.

screens.title: Different Sources of Risk
screens.content: One company may struggle. An entire industry may slow down. Markets may fall together, while cash can lose purchasing power over time.
screens.illustration: Four risk cards show a company problem, industry slowdown, market decline, and rising prices.

screens.title: Spread, Then Stress-Test
screens.content: Your task is to spread the money and observe how different problems affect concentrated and diversified portfolios.
screens.illustration: The allocation board connects to two test buttons: One Company Falls and Whole Market Falls.

screens.title: Which Plan Depends Least on One Outcome?
screens.question: Which allocation is least dependent on the result of one company?

options.text: Rs. 10,000 in one company
options.response: This is highly concentrated. One company’s result can strongly affect the whole portfolio.

options.text: Rs. 10,000 across four companies in one industry
options.response: This spreads money across companies, but all four may still be affected by the same industry problem.

options.text: Money across different companies, cash, and a broad fund
options.response: This reduces dependence on one company or one type of outcome, although losses are still possible.

options.text: Rs. 10,000 in cash
options.response: Cash may reduce short-term price changes, but the plan remains concentrated in one asset type and faces inflation risk.

screens.title: Build and Stress-Test the Portfolio
screens.instruction: Allocate ten Rs. 1,000 tokens. Then test how your portfolio responds when one company or the wider market performs badly.

The learner allocates money in Rs. 1,000 steps.

The several-companies option contains four companies from different industries in this activity.
The diversified fund is assumed to hold a broad mix of investments.
Cash does not change during the short classroom stress tests.

Fees, taxes, dividends, interest, and currency changes are excluded.

Diversification may reduce some risks but cannot guarantee profit or prevent loss.

screens.title: Reduce Dependence, Not Every Risk
screens.content: You saw how one company’s fall had a larger effect when all Rs. 10,000 depended on it. Diversification means spreading money across different investments and asset types so one result has less influence. Meaningful diversification also considers industries and risk sources, not only the number of holdings. It can reduce concentration risk, but markets, inflation, interest rates, currencies, or several investments falling together can still cause losses. Diversification manages risk; it does not guarantee safety or higher returns.
screens.simpleSummary: Spread exposure to reduce concentration, not to guarantee profit.
screens.illustration: One concentrated tower splits into several smaller towers, while a wider market-risk cloud remains above all of them.

screens.title: More Than Several Company Names

reviewChecklist.notes: The mission focuses on diversification as a method for reducing concentration risk.
The mission distinguishes company-specific, industry, market, inflation, interest-rate, and currency risks.
The mission uses adult investment decisions, cash, funds, industries, inflation, and portfolio allocation without advanced technical language.
The allocations and scoring thresholds are clearly labelled as fictional classroom examples rather than real recommendations.
The mission repeatedly states that diversification cannot guarantee profit or prevent loss.
The mission uses fictional percentage shocks only to demonstrate concentration and does not predict real market movements.
Concentrated, cash-heavy, and diversified allocations are explained through trade-offs without judging the learner.
The mission explains meaningful diversification, correlated investments, cash risk, market-wide declines, and risks diversification cannot remove.
The mission uses PKR, Rs. 10,000, companies, cash, funds, banks, property businesses, and familiar adult financial decisions in Pakistan.
The learner allocates money, receives concentration feedback, and compares company-specific and market-wide stress tests.
The quiz addresses guaranteed protection, same-industry concentration, cash concentration, and meaningful diversification.

reviewChecklist.item: Mission can be completed in under five minutes
reviewChecklist.notes: The mission uses three short story screens, ten quick allocation tokens, three follow-up questions, and three quiz questions.

reviewChecklist.item: Language matches the target reading level
reviewChecklist.notes: The language is practical, clear, respectful, and suitable for beginner adults.
